boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Elizabethtown College traditions spanning orientation, seasonal celebrations, service, signature food, songs, and milestone ceremonies.

cards.title: Walk Into Town With the New Class
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation meets downtown Elizabethtown
cards.notes: Join the incoming class on its orientation walk downtown, then use the route to learn local businesses and meet classmates.
cards.short_summary: New Blue Jays begin college by walking together into the surrounding town.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College identifies the First-Year Walk as a fall orientation highlight in which new students walk downtown, visit businesses, and meet peers.
cards.access_notes: Organized for new students during fall orientation; consult the current orientation schedule for timing and participation details.

cards.title: Say TGIS When Spring Finally Arrives
cards.subtitle: An April campus weekend dating to 1974
cards.notes: Watch Student Activities announcements in April for outdoor games, performances, and the festival staged on Brinser Field.
cards.short_summary: Etown welcomes spring with a weekend whose initials have become their own campus vocabulary.
cards.evidence_claim: The College documents Thank Goodness It's Spring Weekend as an annual April tradition begun on April 5, 1974, featuring activities, performances, and a Brinser Field festival.
cards.access_notes: Held in April and sponsored by the Office of Student Activities; confirm the current program and venue access before attending.

cards.title: Go From Holiday Feast to Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: A paired celebration before Thanksgiving break
cards.notes: Follow the campus sequence from Dining Services' holiday meal to the tree lighting, hot chocolate, cookies, and carols.
cards.short_summary: The campus starts its winter celebration before Thanksgiving with dinner, lights, and singing.
cards.evidence_claim: The College says Dining Services prepares a holiday feast before Thanksgiving break, followed by a Student Assembly-sponsored tree lighting with hot chocolate, cookies, and carols.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled before Thanksgiving break for the campus community; consult current campus announcements for location and eligibility.

cards.title: Take Home the Hospitality Cake
cards.subtitle: A campus welcome custom established in 1974
cards.notes: Look for the College's carrot cake at campus events; prospective students still receive a piece to take home after visiting.
cards.short_summary: A president's favorite dessert became Etown's edible symbol of hospitality.
cards.evidence_claim: The College reports that President Morley J. Mays made carrot cake synonymous with Etown hospitality and that prospective students still take a piece home.
cards.access_notes: The official page documents distribution to prospective students and appearances at campus events; availability outside those settings is not guaranteed.

cards.title: Enter the Academic Year in Procession
cards.subtitle: The formal welcome for each incoming class
cards.notes: Attend Convocation to see faculty and administrators process in regalia before the president formally addresses the incoming class.
cards.short_summary: Etown opens its academic year by inducting the newest class amid full academic ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College states that Convocation begins the academic year with a regalia procession, incoming-class induction, and presidential address.
cards.access_notes: Part of the College's institutional calendar; confirm the current ceremony time and guest-access rules with the College.

cards.title: Pass the Flame to the Junior Class
cards.subtitle: A candlelight handoff on Commencement eve
cards.notes: Observe the senior reflections and symbolic transfer of the flame to junior class officers inside Leffler Chapel.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors entrust a literal flame to the class following behind them.
cards.evidence_claim: The College documents Baccalaureate as a candlelight service in Leffler Chapel on the night before Commencement, including a flame passed from seniors to junior class officers.
cards.access_notes: Held in Leffler Chapel and Performance Center the night before Commencement; verify current guest admission and seating arrangements.

cards.title: Graduate Outdoors in the Dell
cards.subtitle: Etown's spring degree ceremony setting
cards.notes: Plan for an outdoor ceremony where graduates join trustees, faculty, administrators, and the 50th-reunion class in procession.
cards.short_summary: Etown turns the Dell into its ceremonial center at the end of spring semester.
cards.evidence_claim: Elizabethtown College says Commencement is held in the Dell at the end of spring and includes the 50th-reunion class in its academic procession.
cards.access_notes: A spring institutional ceremony; consult the current Commencement site for tickets, weather contingencies, and guest procedures.

cards.title: Follow the Floats Down College Avenue
cards.subtitle: The annual Homecoming route through campus
cards.notes: Claim a safe viewing place along College Avenue and watch student- and staff-built floats move through Homecoming weekend.
cards.short_summary: Campus groups translate Etown memories and themes into a moving line of homemade floats.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies the College Avenue parade as part of annual Homecoming; its 2024 anniversary recap documents the 29th parade with student- and staff-built floats.
cards.access_notes: Held during fall Homecoming and Family Weekend; review the current schedule and any College Avenue traffic restrictions before arrival.

cards.title: Sing the Gray-and-Blue Refrain
cards.subtitle: A 1909 alumna's song, refreshed in 2024
cards.notes: Use the College-published words when the alma mater is sung, including its refrain linking service with Etown's colors.
cards.short_summary: A song written by a 1909 graduate now carries updated words into Etown ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: The College credits the alma mater to Jennie Miller Via, Class of 1909, and says a campus committee refreshed its lyrics during the 2024 125th anniversary.
cards.access_notes: The lyrics are publicly posted by the College; particular performances depend on the schedule and access rules of the hosting ceremony.

cards.title: Turn One Day Into Community Service
cards.subtitle: A college-wide service tradition launched in 1994
cards.notes: Register through the College when opportunities open, then follow the assigned community partner's instructions for the service day.
cards.short_summary: Blue Jays leave campus together for a coordinated day of work with community partners.
cards.evidence_claim: The College records Into the Streets as a college-wide community-service program inaugurated with nearly 400 students in 1994 and calls it a longstanding tradition.
cards.access_notes: Participation is organized by the College and may involve off-campus partner sites; use current registration and transportation instructions.
